newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bendigo expects profit in line with 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bendigo expects profit in line with 1996.

text.p: Victorian-based regional bank Bendigo Bank Ltd said on Thursday it expected its after tax profit excluding abnormals to be much in line with last year's result despite adjustments to its asset base in the wake of home loan margin pressures.
In 1995/96 financial year the bank reported a net profit of A$12.8 million.
In a statement, managing director Rob Hunt said the changes in asset base meant a reduced proportion of on-balance sheet assets in residential lending.
"Just on 60 percent of our loans are now for residential purposes, a major shift within 12 months," Hunt said.

Contributing to the shift in asset base were a growth in the bank's commercial lending, the acquisition of Monte Paschi Australia's A$400 million loan book and the removal of parts of the business that no longer contributed to profitability.
By 3.05 p.m. (0505 GMT), Bendigo bank shares were three cents lower at A$4.45 on light turnover of 17,584 shares.
